guarantees.claim: encode_bytepad is always combinatinally driven by the function encode_bytepad_len with input strength_i.
prefix is always the concatenation {ns_data_i, encode_bytepad}.
prefix_sliced is a slice of the full prefix vector selected by prefix_index via the prim_slicer instance.
When masking is enabled, prefix_data[0] is assigned to all zeros and prefix_data[1] is assigned to prefix_sliced.
When masking is disabled, prefix_data[0] is assigned to prefix_sliced; no other share index is driven.

assumptions.claim: The combined prefix (ns_data_i concatenated with encode_bytepad) is always smaller than the block size (168 or 136 bits).
assumptions.risk: If violated, slicing or indexing may span beyond the intended message area, causing incorrect padding or data corruption.

assumptions.claim: prefix_index is always a valid index within the range defined by PrefixSize*8 / MsgWidth slices.
assumptions.risk: An out-of-range select may produce invalid output or X in simulation, potentially leaking previous state or breaking control.

uncertain_points.claim: When EnMasking is low but Share > 1, prefix_data[1] is left undriven. This could propagate an uninitialized or floating value to masked datapath consumers.
uncertain_points.risk: Secret shares may be uninitialized or deterministically zero, breaking masked SCA countermeasures and possibly exposing secret material.

uncertain_points.claim: The size constraint on the prefix (smaller than block size) is only an implicit assumption; no RTL checker enforces it. ns_data_i width is parameterizable and may violate the assumption in some configurations.
uncertain_points.cond: ns_data_i length combined with encode_bytepad exceeds block size
uncertain_points.risk: Prefix data may be truncated, misaligned, or overflow into subsequent data, causing non-standard padding or message corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: The function encode_bytepad_len(strength_i) is used but its implementation is not visible in this chunk. The correctness of the resulting encode_bytepad is essential for SHA3 prefix alignment.
uncertain_points.cond: strength_i takes a value that the function interprets incorrectly
uncertain_points.risk: A wrong bytepad encoding leads to non‑compliant padding, potentially breaking protocol interop or enabling side‑channel distinguishers.
